subject: MedTech Labs — capacity, SLOs, and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@medtechlabs.com>, Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@medtechlabs.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: MedTech Labs — capacity, SLOs, and next steps

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete asks we agreed to move forward with. I wanted to capture the core constraints so we can make the technical deep-dive efficient.

Pain points we heard
- Real-time triage service must return results quickly: 95th percentile latency target <= 300ms for short requests (~<256 tokens).
- End-to-end throughput requirement during daytime peaks: sustained 800 req/s with bursts up to ~2k req/s for short windows (~10–15 minutes).
- Some requests are heavy (document summarization) that can tolerate higher latency but require larger context (up to 4k tokens).
- Data residency & auditability: logs for inference requests must be retained 12 months and be exportable for security audits.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II and KMS integration mandatory; private network/VPC preferred for production.

Model/serving constraints we discussed
- Lightweight triage model (client-side routing to model A) for classification and short-form responses.
- Larger summarization model (model B) for batch/async summarization pipelines.
- Expect average payload size: 600–900 bytes; token distribution skewed toward short requests but ~12% of requests will be long-context summarizations.

Proposed deployment topology (initial recommendation)
- Dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west with autoscaling and burst capacity enabled.
- Private VPC peering + customer-managed NAT for egress controls.
- Prefix/KV caching for triage endpoints; separate pool/queue for batch summarization to avoid head-of-line latency.

Immediate asks / action items for MedTech Labs
1) Confirm representative payload samples (2–3 JSONs): average triage request + 1 long document summarization example.
2) Confirm whether 95th p50/95/99 latency targets are for wall-clock to user or purely model inference time.
3) Provide procurement contact and preferred contract cadence (PO vs. DocuSign).

Attachments: draft SOW and a quick network sketch for reference (stubs attached).

Next step: propose a technical deep-dive with your infra and security (we suggest 60–90 minutes) to lock topology, KV/cache sizing, and SLO scoping. I’m suggesting Thursday Oct 7 or Friday Oct 8 — if you prefer earlier, we can open a slot next week.

Thanks — next email will include an agenda for the deep-dive if the times above work.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0112

From: Samir Patel <samir@medtechlabs.com>

Subject: Re: MedTech Labs — capacity, SLOs, and next steps

Jordan —

Appreciate the thorough summary. Confirming the items below:

- Latency: user-facing requirement is 95th <= 300ms (includes network egress within our VPC to Redwood endpoint). Model-only time target can be looser; we want the end-to-end number to be our SLA.
- Throughput: 800 req/s sustained, bursts to 2k for short spikes — those numbers are correct.
- Payload samples: attaching two sample payloads (triage_short.json, summarization_long.json).
- Compliance: Procurement will want a SOC2 summary and our security team will require a KMS diagram. I’ve attached a SOC2 extract and our initial network DMZ diagram.

Procurement contact: procurement@medtechlabs.com (cc'd). We typically prefer DocuSign for NDAs/SOWs.

We can do Wednesday Oct 6 or Monday Oct 11 for a technical deep-dive; our infra lead (Elena) prefers Oct 6 afternoon PT.

Owners assigned above; please reply to this thread if owners need to shift. I’ve attached the current draft SOW and the SOC2 extract for your security review; procurement — feel free to share standard terms if you want us to pre-seed contract language.
